text.en: Meena asked her teacher, "Is every number a fraction?" The teacher smiled and wrote the square root of 2.

Rational numbers can be written as p/q with q not zero, and their decimals either end or repeat. Irrational numbers cannot be written like this, and their decimals neither end nor repeat, as with the square root of 2 and pi. Together rational and irrational numbers form the real numbers, which fill the number line.
The radical notation n-th root of a is written with a radical sign. A surd is an irrational root such as the square root of 3. Simplify surds before adding or subtracting. Like surds use the same radical part. In the positive square-root examples here, we can multiply by multiplying their radicands. Rationalisation rewrites a fraction with a rational denominator by multiplying numerator and denominator by a suitable nonzero factor. For a two-term square-root denominator, a conjugate can help.
For a positive number, scientific notation uses a coefficient at least one and less than ten, multiplied by ten raised to an integer power.

For a positive number, scientific notation uses a coefficient at least one and less than ten, multiplied by ten raised to an integer power.
Write an integer as a fraction over one. For example, negative seven equals negative seven divided by one. Every integer therefore fits the rational-number definition.
Find a rational number between two and three by averaging them. The mean is five halves. Applying the same idea again produces more rational numbers in ever smaller intervals.
Reduce a fraction before testing whether its decimal ends. Three over forty already has no common factor to cancel. Its denominator is a product of powers of two and five.
Multiply numerator and denominator by twenty-five to get seventy-five thousandths. The decimal ends because the denominator can be turned into a power of ten.
One sixth has a factor three in its reduced denominator, so its decimal continues with a repeating digit. In long division, a repeated remainder makes the next digits repeat too.
To turn zero point four five repeating into a fraction, rename it x. Multiplying by one hundred shifts exactly one repeat block to the left of the decimal point.
Subtract the original x to cancel the repeating part. Ninety-nine x equals forty-five, so x is forty-five over ninety-nine, which reduces to five elevenths.
For square root of two, square the numbers one point four and one point five. Their squares are one point nine six and two point two five. This puts the root between them.
Let us see why square root of two is irrational. Suppose square root of two were a fraction in lowest terms. Squaring would require the numerator to be even.
An even numerator would make its square a multiple of four. In the same equation this forces the denominator to be even as well. That contradicts the claim that the fraction was in lowest terms.

text.en: Use the radical index to name the root. The cube root of twenty-seven is three because three cubed gives twenty-seven. The same number can be written with the exponent one third.
For a positive square root, look for perfect-square factors. Seventy-two is thirty-six times two, so its square root simplifies to six times the square root of two.
Compare square root of fifty with three square root of two. Fifty is twenty-five times two, so the first term becomes five square root of two.
The two simplified terms now share the same radical part. Subtract their coefficients, five minus three, leaving two square root of two.
For multiplication, square root of three times square root of twelve becomes square root of thirty-six, which is six. Both factors are irrational, and the product is rational in this example.
For one over the square root of five, multiply above and below by the square root of five. The new denominator is five and the new numerator is square root of five.
A denominator of square root of three minus one has two terms. Try its conjugate, square root of three plus one. The middle products cancel when you multiply.
Multiplying a numerator and denominator by the same nonzero value leaves the fraction’s value unchanged. Here the new numerator is square root of three plus one, and the denominator is two.
Write seventy-two thousand three hundred as seven point two three times ten raised to four. Check by moving the decimal four places to the right when converting back.
Write zero point zero zero zero four two as four point two times ten raised to minus four. The negative exponent shows division by ten four times.

For multiplication in scientific notation, multiply the coefficients and add the powers of ten. Three times four gives twelve. Move one factor of ten into the exponent so the coefficient returns to standard form.

Finish by sorting your answers. Ask whether you used a fraction test, an exact radical form or an approximation for location. A decimal bound helps place a surd while its radical preserves the exact value.

why.en: The two middle products cancel and the denominator becomes two.

why.en: The expression has the same value and its denominator is rational.

prompt.en: A friend says Every real number is rational. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: Numbers like the square root of 2 are irrational.

points.en: Irrational decimals never end or repeat.
Rationalisation clears a surd in the denominator.
